title: Stekt tjäder (Roasted Grouse)
description: Prepared with grouse, lard, and broth or cream.
steps: Pluck and singe the grouse, remove organs, rinse well and dry. If it has been frozen, soak it in milk overnight.
Lard it with lard cut into fine strips and truss.
Heat the butter in a roasting pan, place the grouse breast-side up, brown well and salt. Cook on low heat and baste occasionally with broth or thin cream.
Roasting takes 2-3 hours.
Strain the meat gravy, skim it, and prepare the sauce according to general rules for sauces.

title: Stekt, Späckad Rensadel (Roasted Larded Reindeer Saddle)
description: Prepared with skimmed milk or milk, lard, and broth.

ingredients.name: 3 litres skimmed milk or drinking milk

steps: Thaw the saddle as the meat in the previous recipe.
Dry it well and carefully remove all membranes, then lard the saddle thickly with finely cut lard strips dipped in salt.

Brown the butter in a roasting pan, place the saddle in with the meat side down and brown it beautifully, then turn it and add liquid, first with the boiling broth, then with the boiling cream or milk, and let it roast with a tightly closed lid until tender, about 2½ hours, basting about every 10 minutes.

Place the saddle on a warm platter, loosen the meat neatly on both sides of the backbone, place on a cutting board and slice across into beautiful slices, which are then reassembled on the saddle so it looks whole.
Garnish with browned potatoes, salad or parsley and serve with lingonberry jelly and reduced sauce (see no. 429).

title: Stekta kycklingar i gryta (Braised Chickens in a Pot)
description: Prepared with chickens, cream, and white pepper.
steps: Clean the chickens, singe them, draw them (see page 299 onwards), rinse well and dry.
Clean the parsley, rinse it, wrap it in a cloth, chop it finely and work it into the butter.
Fill the chickens with the parsley butter, sew them closed, rub them with salt and truss them.
Brown the butter in an iron pot, add the birds together with the giblets (necks, livers and hearts) and brown well on all sides over gentle heat.

title: Stekta Rapphöns (Roasted Partridges)
description: Prepared with partridges, lard, and bouillon.
steps: Young partridges are recognized by their yellow legs, whereas older ones have a reddish color. Old partridges should hang longer than young ones and require longer roasting time, but the meat is equally juicy and good as from young birds.
If the partridges are frozen, thaw them overnight in a warm kitchen, clean them (see page 299) and let them lie in lukewarm milk for a few hours.
Remove, let them drain, dry well, truss and cover with thin lard slices.

Brown them in the butter together with the giblets, salt and add first the boiling bouillon, then the cream, and let them slowly roast with a tight lid until tender, or 1—1¼ hours; baste them frequently.
If the partridges are young and not frozen, they should not lie in milk and should not be covered with lard. They are roasted in plenty of butter as previously stated.
If desired, they can be diluted with only bouillon or cream.
Cut, garnish (see page 300) and serve with the reduced sauce or with strained sauce (see recipe 429). Mushrooms can be sautéed in butter and added to the sauce.

title: Svartsoppa (Black Soup)
description: A soup made with giblets, goose or pork or blood, and broth.

ingredients.name: 1/2 liter broth in which the giblets were cooked

steps: The giblets consist of head, neck, wing tips, feet, heart, liver and stomach.

Scald the head in hot water, split lengthwise, rinse well, remove the eyes and scrape the beak.

Carefully loosen the gallbladder from the liver, which is used for goose liver sausage.
Remove the neck skin and use as sausage casing.
Break the neck, scald the wing tips and split them.
Rinse the giblets well and preferably let them soak in water for a few hours.
Place them in 1 liter of cold water, skim well, add 1/2 tablespoon of the salt and 6 white peppercorns and 4 cloves and let everything cook with a tightly closed lid about 3 hours.
Rinse the prunes well in lukewarm water, place in 3 deciliters of cold water together with 1 tablespoon of the sugar and cook until soft.
Ten minutes before they are done, add the apples, peeled and cut into quarters.
When the meat is tender, take it out, cut into pieces and place in the soup bowl.
Strain the broth, skim it and let it boil down to 1/2 liter.
Strain the blood and whisk with the flour and 1/2 liter of the cold broth; this mixture should stand and swell for 1 hour.
Add the blood mixture to the hot broth, stirring constantly, then add the remaining sugar, vinegar and the cooked prunes with apples and let the soup cook a few minutes.
Season with white pepper and sherry and serve with fried goose liver.

title: Syltade gurkor (Pickled Cucumbers)
description: Prepared with cucumbers, vinegar, and white pepper.

ingredients.name: 5 st. stora gurkor med ej för stort kärnhus (5 large cucumbers with not too large seeds)

steps: Gurkorna skalas och skäras itu på längden.
Allt inkråm gräves ut med en silversked, och gurk- halvorna skäras itu på bredden.
Vattnet kokas upp med saltet.
Så många gurkor, som få rum på ytan, läggas i och få koka, tills de bli mjuka och klara.
De tagas då upp med hålslev och läggas på dubbelt linne att rinna av.
Ättikan och sockret kokas med kryddorna, inknutna i en liten muslinslapp, till en lag.
Då lagen har stark kryddsmak, lyftes den av elden.
Gurkorna läggas ned i en porslinskruka, och lagen silas över.
Burken täckes över med fyrdubbelt linne och en tallrik.
Kryddorna tillvaratagas.
Efter 3–4 dagar hälles lagen av och kokas tillsammans med kryddorna omkr. 10 min.
Den slås därefter upp att kallna och silas sedan åter över gurkorna.
Kryddorna tillvaratagas.
Efter 6 dagar förnyas samma kokning.
Den upprepas ånyo efter åtta dagar, och gurkorna äro färdiga.
Är lagen för stark, bör man vid sista kokningen tillsätta litet vatten.

title: Syltade Gurkor (Preserved Cucumbers)
description: Prepared with cucumbers, vinegar, and white pepper.

ingredients.name: 5 large cucumbers with not too large seed cavities
For the brine: 2 liters good vinegar

steps: Peel the cucumbers and cut them in half lengthwise.
Carefully scoop out all the insides with a silver spoon and cut the cucumber halves in half widthwise.
Boil the water with the salt.
Place as many cucumbers as fit on the surface and let them cook until soft and clear.
Remove them with a skimmer and place on doubled linen to drain.
Cook the vinegar and sugar with the spices, tied in a small muslin bag, into a brine.
When the brine has a strong spice flavor, remove it from heat.
Place the cucumbers in a porcelain crock and strain the brine over.
Cover the crock with quadruple linen and a plate.
Save the spices.
After 3-4 days pour off the brine and cook it together with the spices for about 10 minutes.
Pour it to cool and then strain it again over the cucumbers.
Save the spices.
After 6 days repeat the same cooking.
Repeat again after eight days, and the cucumbers are ready.
If the brine is too strong, one should add a little water at the final cooking.
Melons and pumpkins are preserved in the same way.

title: Syltade hallon (Preserved Raspberries)
description: Prepared with raspberries, sugar, and water.
steps: Clean the raspberries.
From the sugar and water, boil a clear syrup that should be so well cooked that a cooled sample threads between the fingers or that a drop on a plate does not immediately run out.
Add the berries, and let the preserve come to a boil, lift off, shake and skim.
Set it back on, let it come to a boil, lift off, shake and skim.
Repeat this 4 to 5 times, or until the berries are clear and the syrup is shimmering.
Shake the preserve until it has cooled somewhat.

title: Syltade jordgubbar (Candied Strawberries)
description: Prepared with strawberries and sugar.
steps: Clean the strawberries, rinse gently and let drain.
Layer the strawberries and granulated sugar alternately in a jam pot, and let them stand to release their juice.
Place the pot over heat, bring the jam to a rapid, brief boil, remove from heat, shake and skim.
Return to heat, bring to a boil, remove from heat, shake and skim.
Repeat this process 3-4 times, or until the berries are clear and the syrup is thick.
Shake the jam while it cools slightly, then immediately pour into prepared jars.
